Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 110, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Idha ja'a nasru Allah﴾ (When the help of Allah comes): i.e., the help of Allah to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) against his polytheist enemies.

Wa'l-fath (and the conquest): i.e., the conquest of Makkah.

Fi dini Allahi afwajan (into the religion of Allah in throngs): i.e., into Islam, group after group.

Fa-sabbih bi-hamdi rabbika (then glorify your Lord with His praise): i.e., declare Him free of any partner, while joining that with praise of Him.

Wa-staghfirhu (and seek His forgiveness): i.e., ask Him for forgiveness, turning to Him in repentance.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾. These three blessed verses were revealed in the last days of the Messenger (ﷺ), and they carry a sign to the Prophet (ﷺ) that his appointed time is near. So His saying, ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾, means: for you, O our Messenger, so that you become victorious over your enemies in every battle you fight against them, and ﴿the conquest﴾ comes to you, which is the conquest of Makkah, which Allah opened for you, and it became a land of Islam after it had been a land of disbelief. ﴿And you see the people﴾ from the inhabitants of Yemen and others ﴿entering into﴾ your religion, the Islamic religion, ﴿in throngs﴾ and groups, group after group, after they had been entering individually, one by one, while fearful. When this has come to pass and you have seen it, ﴿then glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, thanking Him for the blessing of victory and conquest, the entry of people into your religion, and the ending of the false religion of the polytheists. ﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾, i.e., ask Him for forgiveness for whatever lapse has come from you which would be a sin in your case, given your nearness and perfection of knowledge; as for others, it is not a sin that one seeks forgiveness for and turns to Allah the Exalted in repentance from. And His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾, means: indeed Allah the Exalted, who commanded you to seek forgiveness, is ever Accepting of repentance toward Him, accepting the repentance of His servants, forgiving their sins and having mercy upon them.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The legitimacy of announcing a person's death to his family, but without public proclamation and raised voice.

2- The obligation of gratitude upon the realization of a blessing, and among that is the prostration of gratitude.

3- The legitimacy of saying "Subhanaka Allahumma wa-bihamdika, Allahumma-ghfir li" in bowing (ruku').
